name: Level match
threading: Pure functions with no shared state: call from any non-real-time thread (the plugin runs them on a worker). They allocate, so never call them from an audio callback.
platforms: Any C++17 compiler. No dependencies at all.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/level_match -B build/level_match && cmake --build build/level_match && ctest --test-dir build/level_match
summary: ITU-R BS.1770-4 integrated loudness (K-weighting, 400 ms blocks with 75 % overlap, absolute and relative gates) and the Level Match gain: the clamped, 0.1 dB rounded gain that brings a generated pattern to the loudness of the loop it came from, with a headroom rule so the match alone can never clip.
public_api: `measure(planar, channels, frames, sampleRate) -> Loudness{lufs, samplePeak, valid}`
`computeMatch(source, pattern, trimDb, limiterOn, ceilingDb) -> MatchResult{gainDb, requestedDb, valid, clamped, headroomLimited}`
limits: Mono or stereo, 8 kHz and up; at least 100 ms of audio; gain clamped to +/-12 dB and rounded to 0.1 dB; mono is measured as if duplicated to both channels
adapters: Render the pattern offline with the loop's own sample rate, measure both, then feed the two `Loudness` values to `computeMatch`.
adapter_notes: The module does no rendering and holds no state; caching and scheduling are the caller's job.
removal: Delete the folder; callers lose Level match only.
